story_type: booster separation seen by long-range tracking cameras
hook: Two giant boosters let go of a Moon rocket with four people aboard.
narration: These are the two boosters of Artemis Two, letting go of a Moon rocket.
It was April first, 2026, at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Four astronauts sat in the Orion capsule on top, headed for the Moon.
Each side booster is a solid rocket. Once it lights, it cannot be shut off.
For about two minutes, the pair gave the rocket more than three quarters of its push.
Then they burned out, and small motors fired to shove them clear. [short pause]
Long-range tracking cameras, miles from the pad, caught every second.
outcome: Both boosters fell away, and Orion flew on with four astronauts toward the Moon.
title: Artemis II boosters break away
description:
On April 1, 2026, NASA's long-range tracking cameras followed the Artemis II launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, through the moment the two solid rocket boosters separated from the Moon rocket carrying four astronauts.

facts.claim: Four astronauts launched on Artemis II from Kennedy on April 1, 2026
facts.source_quote: Four astronauts aboard NASA’s Orion spacecraft atop the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket launch on the agency’s Artemis II test flight, Wednesday, April 1, 2026, from Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. ET.
